flops_independent_recompute.tool: challenge/export/compute_flops.py run by B3 on a clean checkout
flops_independent_recompute.caveat: same tool, so this proves reproducibility, not method independence; the denominator definition is still a team decision

behaviour_level.method: zero one input modality at a time, decode through StudentPlanAdapter, compare behaviour sequence with the full-input baseline
behaviour_level.reading: a higher change share means the model relies on that modality for its plan; near-zero means removing it does not change the plan

multimodal_ablation.reading: Zeroing state changes the model massively (worst-head cosine 0.4654, behaviour relative change 71.6 percent, argmax flips in 122 of 150 cases). Zeroing rgb, text_tokens or targets barely moves the logits (cosines 0.9544-0.9930, relative change 3-10 percent) and never flips the decoded behaviour. So on this candidate the plan is dominated by the state encoder and the three other modalities contribute only marginally at decision level.
multimodal_ablation.caveat: Zeroing is not the same as removing evidence: a black image is still an image and zero tokens are still a token sequence. The number measures sensitivity to replacing a modality with its zero value.

anomalous_input_suite.mismatch: empty_source_text expected MUST_FAIL_CLOSED but a plan was produced
